Find applicable evidence-backed ways to reduce execution time in this GitHub Actions workflow. Consider its jobs, dependencies, commands, triggers, and repository manifests.
name: CI

# Controls when the workflow will run
on: ['push', 'pull_request', 'workflow_dispatch']

jobs:
  # Security audits run in a separate job, so a new finding shows up as its
  # own failing check without keeping the test suites below from running to
  # completion. Dependency advisories are published independently of our
  # code, so a new one can turn any build red overnight; a new Brakeman
  # finding needs reviewing, but shouldn't hold back the test results.
  security-audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: setup Ruby
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
           ruby-version: 3.4.8
           bundler-cache: true

      - name: setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'yarn'

      # Fails when Gemfile.lock contains a gem with a published security
      # advisory (ruby-advisory-db, refreshed on each run).
      - name: Ruby dependency vulnerability audit
        run: bundle exec bundle-audit check --update

      # Mirrors the Ruby audit for the JavaScript dependency tree: fails
      # when yarn.lock resolves a package with a published npm advisory of
      # moderate severity or higher. `--recursive` covers transitive
      # dependencies, where nearly all such advisories land. Advisories that
      # have been reviewed and don't apply are listed, with the reasoning, in
      # npmAuditIgnoreAdvisories in .yarnrc.yml. Reads the lockfile directly,
      # so it needs no `yarn install`. Runs even when the Ruby audit fails,
      # so both sets of advisories show up at once.
      - name: JavaScript dependency vulnerability audit
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: yarn npm audit --recursive --severity moderate

      # Security static analysis. Fails on any finding that is not in
      # config/brakeman.ignore, where every baselined warning carries a
      # written justification. A new finding means either a real issue or a
      # pattern that needs reviewing and, if genuinely safe, adding to the
      # baseline with its reasoning -- not a blanket suppression. Runs even
      # when the dependency audits fail.
      - name: Ruby security static analysis
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: bundle exec brakeman --no-pager -q -i config/brakeman.ignore

  build:
    # The type of runner that the job will run on
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    env:
      SECRET_KEY_BASE: ci_secret_key_base_not_used_for_real_sessions

    # Use native service containers instead of standalone actions
    # to avoid Docker Hub rate limits and Docker client version mismatches.
    services:
      redis:
        image: redis:7
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

          --health-retries 5

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
